content:
We have mass spectrum data. Need to identify elements definitively based on isotope distribution patterns visible. Look at peaks: m/z values around 231-240. Likely isotopic pattern of chlorine (Cl-35/37) shows ~2:1 ratio, but here spacing ~2 Da? Actually Cl isotopes differ by 2 Da. Bromine also 2 Da. But pattern: peaks at 231.96544, 232.96883 (+1.00339), 233.96320 (+0.99437), 234.96657 (+1.00337), 235.96061 (+0.99404), etc. This looks like isotopic pattern of carbon (13C) spacing ~1.00335 Da. So many peaks spaced by ~1 Da, typical for high-resolution isotopic envelope of a molecule with many carbons. Also presence of peaks at +2 Da etc. Need to identify elements that can be definitively identified from pattern: Carbon (C) due to 13C pattern. Possibly Sulfur (S) has isotopes 32,33,34,36 with distinct pattern but spacing ~1-2 Da and relative intensities. But we need to see if pattern matches S? The pattern shows many peaks with decreasing intensity, typical of many carbons. Sulfur would give a distinct M+2 peak about 4% intensity relative to M. Not obvious.

We can retrieve isotopic distribution to compare.
